_comment: instance_id -> what that producing instance MEANS here. A producer states an identity it cannot falsify and says nothing about its meaning; this file is where the meaning lives. Only `class` is read by code — role, name, note and registered_at are for people, and nothing branches on them. An identity that is not listed resolves to `unknown`, which is a rule rather than a setting: `unknown` is refused for a measurement run once the gate is armed. Keys are 12 lowercase hex and are refused in any other shape, because a key that cannot match leaves its data `unknown` without saying so. TRACKED COPY — it carries the schema and the identities this gate is meant to admit, development and production alike. An identity is an opaque minted string and nothing about it is secret; what stays out of here is anything ABOUT the machine that holds it (an account number, a terminal path). user_configs/data_origins.json still takes precedence and is where an operator keeps a claim they do not want published.

It is minted per SCHEMA rather than per database, because their test schema lives inside the production database and journal_id alone therefore cannot separate two producers. Verified from THREE sources before registering: stated on the bus, answered by GET /v1/health from here, and carried on the envelopes of all three streams. First stamped `seq` per stream — crypto_sentiment 4420, forex_macro_sentiment 4269, crypto_sentiment_nano 14; everything below carries no identity and resolves to `unknown`, which is the truthful answer and NOT a claim that the same producer wrote it. `stream_epoch` stayed 1 across the deploy, so no cursor rewound. A schema CLONED from production keeps this id until someone re-mints it and no guard can see that, which is why re-minting is part of standing a copy up.

attestations._comment: A dated claim about files written before their producer could state an identity. It is a PREDICATE, not a list, because the archive keeps growing until the block ships — and it closes itself the moment it does. The grade is assigned by the resolver and is always `attested`, never `stamped`. THE SCOPE BELOW COVERS NOTHING (0.0.0 matches no file): the real claim is the operator's and belongs in user_configs/. When writing it, note that the boundary is 1.5.0 and NOT 1.6.0 — no production file will ever carry 1.6.0 (the collector goes 1.5.0 -> 1.7.0 in one step), while DEVELOPMENT files at 1.6.0 do exist and must not be swept in.
